edges.rationale: The client/server process distinction in 'Processes Communicating' builds directly on the client-server architecture concept; you must know what a client-server design is before classifying which side of a communication is the client or server process.

Transport services are defined as what the transport layer offers to an application through its socket; understanding the socket as the application-transport interface (from 'Processes Communicating') is needed to make sense of services delivered to an application.

edges.dependent: Transport Services Provided by the Internet
edges.rationale: The TCP/UDP discussion is an evaluation of the Internet's transport models against the four requirement classes (reliability, throughput, timing, security); the requirement classes must be defined first for the comparison and the SSL/TLS motivation to be meaningful.

An application-layer protocol specifies the types, syntax, semantics, and send/respond rules for messages exchanged between processes; this definition presupposes the process-communication and socket model.
